title: Lacuna Conduit Partnership Framing Call
summary: Introductory call to scope a channel/integration partnership between Redwood Inference and Lacuna Conduit. Covered integration models (marketplace listing vs managed onramp), VPC/private deployment requirements, security (KMS/HSM, SOC2, audit logs), pilot and benchmarking approach, and a tentative onboarding timeline. Customer is most concerned about data residency, predictable latency for inferencing at scale, and tight billing/usage propagation for partner leads.
topics: partnership model: managed onramp vs marketplace listing
integration touchpoints: SDKs, routing, and lead flows
action_items: Maya Chen - Send partner integration one-pager, sample SOW template, and onboarding checklist (due: 2026-07-12)
Samir Patel - Share lightweight benchmark plan + sample perf script for latency/throughput (due: 2026-07-14)
Diego Marquez - Provide Lacuna's network diagram and baseline QPS expectations (due: 2026-07-09)
Priya Singh - Confirm internal stakeholders and preferred commercial model (due: 2026-07-13)
next_steps: Redwood to share security/compliance pack and partner checklist
Customer to validate VPC/hybrid options and provide contact for networking deep dive
Agree on benchmark metrics and success criteria for the POC
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-07-07 16:00 PDT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Ravi Malhotra (Redwood SE); Aisha Rahman (CTO, Lacuna), Diego Marquez (Head of Infra), Priya Singh (Partner Ops), Tom Becker (ML Platform)

Auto-generated summary: Intro call to understand Lacuna Conduit interest in partnering to offer a managed onramp for Redwood-hosted inference and private deploy options. Discussed security and network constraints, initial pilot scope, and next steps.

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, really appreciate you making the time. Quick round robin, then we'll jump into how Redwood typically partners and what paths we can take.
[00:12] Aisha: Hi, I'm Aisha, CTO at Lacuna. We're building a gateway for regulated data workloads, so security and residency are big for us.
[00:19] Diego: Diego here, infra lead. We run mixed cloud and on-prem clusters, so network peering and private link stuff is important.
[00:27] Maya: Great. Samir, want to give quick intro on the technical side?
[00:31] Samir: Yeah hi, Samir Patel, platform SE. I focus on inference performance and integrations — batching, kv cache, quantized models, things like that.
[00:38] Tom: Tom from our ML infra team. We'll own the pilot on our side.
[00:42] Priya: And I'm Priya, partners ops. I'll be coordinating approvals and SLAs.

[00:50] Maya: Cool. High level: two primary partnership patterns we see — marketplace-style listing where Lacuna can route customers directly to Redwood hosted APIs and a managed onramp model where Lacuna bundles Redwood Dedicated/Private as part of its offering. Curious which sounds like the priority?
[01:05] Aisha: For go-to-market, marketplace is nice, but for our enterprise customers we need predictable latency and data isolation — so managed onramp / private deployment is more interesting.

[01:18] Samir: Totally makes sense. For private deployments we offer a customer-controlled control plane or a VPC peering approach with KMS integration. We can support HSM-backed keys if you need FIPS/HSM.
[01:30] Diego: Can you clarify how the KMS/HSM integration works with private deploys? Do keys live in our cloud account or Redwood's?
[01:39] Samir: Preferably in your account — we do bring an agent that talks to your KMS via IAM roles. We avoid copying keys. There's an option where customers host the keys entirely and we only have encrypted tokens, but that adds ops friction.
[01:52] Diego: Ok that helps. Network wise we need to understand egress patterns, peering, and whether we can keep traffic inside our VPC.
[02:01] Maya: We have options: VPC peering, PrivateLink, and an on-prem package with an air-gapped binary for extremely regulated customers.

[02:12] Aisha: What's the latency story? Our SLAs often require p99 under 200ms for short-form generation.
[02:20] Samir: Depends a lot on model, sequence length, and batch strategy. For hosted Redwood endpoints with optimized kernels we routinely hit ~80-120ms p99 for 512-token-ish workloads on our mid-tier models. For Dedicated private placements, latency is even more predictable because you pin capacity. But the trade-off is cost.
[02:38] Tom: When you say optimized kernels, are those available in private deploys too? Or is that only in your hosted fleet?
[02:46] Samir: They are part of the runtime; when we ship private deployments we include the same runtime that picks kernels based on hardware heuristics. That said, some very vendor-specific optimizations (like custom vendor kernels) may be limited depending on the GPUs you have.
[02:58] Diego: We run a mix — older Ampere nodes and some newer H100-ish stuff from our partners. Does Redwood support mixed GPU fleets?
[03:07] Samir: Yes, we can route by policy. You can configure routing for latency vs cost. If an H100 is available we route there; if not, fall back to a quantized variant on Ampere.

[03:20] Maya: Quick note: Lacuna mentioned data residency. Do you have specific regions we need to be aware of?
[03:25] Aisha: We need EU-only data for some customers, and some UK-only requirements too.
[03:30] Maya: We can pin regions and provide regional-only model variants. We also support audit logs and retention controls for Private deployments.

[03:42] Priya: On the commercial side, how do partner leads flow? If we onboard an enterprise and we sell Redwood as a managed layer, how's billing and attribution handled?
[03:51] Maya: Two main patterns: referral fee with tracked lead attribution (we integrate with partner portals) or a co-sell/reseller model where Lacuna invoices and Redwood invoices Lacuna wholesale. We can support both; we also have an integration where usage data and token-level billing can be pushed through an API for reconciliation.
[04:10] Priya: Ok we'll need to see sample invoicing and the lead attribution flow.

[04:17] Samir: Back to tech — for the pilot we usually recommend a small footprint test: 1) baseline traffic replay of representative calls; 2) run throughput and latency tests with our perf harness; 3) validate KV/prefix caching and batching on realistic prompts.
[04:32] Tom: On the traffic replay, can we run it inside our VPC so we don't send customer data out?
[04:37] Samir: Yes, we can run the perf harness inside your environment against a Private deployment. For hosted endpoints we'd sanitize inputs or use synthetic but representative traces.

[04:47] Aisha: A question about caching — we saw mention of a KV cache, can you explain how stateful convo caching interacts with multi-tenant setups?
[04:56] Samir: Sure. Our KV cache stores KV pairs per conversation and can be pinned to a tenant. For shared fleets we namespace the cache so tenant isolation is maintained. In private deployments the KV cache runs locally so there's no cross-tenant leakage.
[05:10] Diego: Is the cache encrypted at rest?
[05:13] Samir: Yes, encrypted at rest; we rotate keys via KMS. In private deployments you control the keys.

[05:20] Maya: I want to call out perf optimizations — quantized variants are useful to reduce cost but you need to validate quality. Redwood Optimize can recommend quantization profiles per model and workload.
[05:33] Tom: Will Redwood Optimize run inside our environment or as a service?
[05:36] Samir: It can be a mix: we can provide recommendations from our hosted analytics but for metrics inside private deployments we can run an offline analysis if you share eval sets or run their metrics locally.

[05:50] [08:00] Speaker 1: (brief hold, background chatter)
[05:55] Aisha: Security/compliance — do you have SOC 2 and ISO certs? And do you provide an evidence pack?
[06:03] Maya: Yes, Redwood is SOC 2 Type II and we have ISO material. We can share the security pack for partners which includes incident response, penetration test summaries, and our data flow diagrams. For private deployments we provide an install checklist and audit logging hooks.
[06:19] Priya: Great, please share that.

[06:24] Diego: A risky point: what about telemetry? Will Redwood collect telemetry from private deployments?
[06:29] Samir: We collect optional telemetry for health checks — you can opt out. For private deployments we can run a push model where only anonymized metrics are shared if you prefer.

[06:39] Tom: For the pilot, what success criteria should we set? Latency, error rate, and cost per 1k tokens?
[06:45] Maya: Yes, common POC metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, throughput (RPS and tokens/sec), error rate and quality metrics (ROUGE/BLEU or human evals for your prompts), and cost per 1k tokens. We'll predefine the thresholds.

[06:59] Aisha: We're also curious about model lifecycle — how do rollouts work? Will we have control over model version pinning?
[07:05] Samir: You can pin versions. We support canary rollouts, A/B tests, and auto-fallback policies. If a model rollout causes degradation we will automatically route to the previous pinned variant per your policy.

[07:18] Maya: Onboarding timeline: if we do a small pilot, we can have an initial network & security review, then spin up a private test deployment in ~2 weeks depending on networking, then run the benchmark for 1-2 weeks. So roughly a month from kickoff to initial validation.
[07:34] Diego: Two weeks for setup — is that assuming Lacuna provides access and network configs promptly?
[07:39] Maya: Yes, that presumes network info and KMS details in week 1. Any delays there push the timeline.

[07:47] Priya: On commercial terms, is there a minimum commit for Dedicated capacity?
[07:52] Maya: For dedicated we typically ask for a monthly baseline commit, but for partner pilots we can be flexible with a short-term reserved pool. We'll follow up with commercial options.

[07:59] Aisha: I want to flag one more requirement — some customers demand the ability to run inference entirely on-prem without any control-plane calls out to the internet. Is an air-gapped option feasible?
[08:09] Samir: We have an on-prem package that supports fully air-gapped inference. There are some limitations: telemetry is local, upgrades are customer-initiated or scheduled with a secure channel, and certain managed features like hosted rollouts aren't available. But we've done that for regulated banks.

[08:26] Tom: For telemetry-less mode, how do we handle model updates and bug fixes?
[08:31] Samir: We provide signed update artifacts and an offline upgrade process. We also provide a patch guidance doc and test harness you can run internally.

[08:41] Diego: Switching gears — how involved is the integration on the SDK side? We have an app layer that needs to call inference endpoints and handle tokenization.
[08:49] Maya: Redwood has SDKs in Python, Go, Java, and a REST/HTTP interface. For partners we typically provide example connectors and a sample integration repo.
[08:58] Tom: Do SDKs handle streaming and function/tool calling?
[09:01] Samir: Yes, streaming is supported in SDKs and we support structured outputs and tool calls. The client will see a consistent interface across hosted and private deployments.

[09:12] Aisha: Any pitfalls customers usually encounter?
[09:15] Samir: Biggest ones: 1) underestimating per-token cost at high throughput without batching; 2) network egress surprises; 3) not validating quantized model quality beforehand. We advise running a small quality regression suite early.

[09:30] Priya: Ok, for next steps we need the security pack, integration one-pager, sample SOW, and the perf script.
[09:38] Maya: We'll share all of that. Samir, you'll attach the perf harness sample?
[09:42] Samir: Yup, I'll send a lightweight bash/python harness plus instructions to run it in VPC.

[09:49] Aisha: One more thing — are there any specific legal terms partners should be aware of for co-sell? Data liability?
[09:56] Maya: We have a partner terms doc and standard Data Processing Addendum (DPA). For regulated customers we negotiate data residency clauses and addendum for on-prem installs. We'll share a redlineable partner package.

[10:08] [10:08] Speaker 2: (brief overlap, someone on mute)

[10:12] Tom: Quick technical question — do you support model quantization to int4 and is that part of the runtime?

[10:17] Samir: We support int8 and experimental int4 depending on model family and hardware. Int4 can be very cost-efficient but quality varies. We'll recommend profiles per model via Redwood Optimize and help validate.

[10:31] Aisha: What's the billing cadence and visibility for partners?

[10:35] Maya: We provide token-level billing with per-route breakdowns, retention windows for usage analytics, and partner portals for aggregated views. Billing cadence can be monthly or net-30 depending on contract.

[10:46] Priya: For initial pilots we prefer a short net-30 invoicing and then move to wholesale monthly billing if the pilot converts.

[10:53] Maya: Sounds reasonable. Any remaining open technical risks?
[10:57] Diego: Network and key management look like the main ones. We'll also validate GPU compatibility with our on-prem nodes.

[11:04] Samir: We'll provide a GPU compatibility matrix and a simple checklist.

[11:10] Maya: Great. I'll recap next steps at the end — but real quick, any requests on demos or deep dives?

[11:16] Aisha: We'd like a dedicated deep dive on private deployment networking and an SE-led perf tune session.
[11:22] Maya: Noted. We'll schedule a network deep dive with Diego and a perf deep dive with Tom and your ML team.

[11:30] Maya: Ok recap — Redwood to send security pack, partner one-pager, sample SOW, perf harness and GPU compatibility matrix. Lacuna to share network diagram, QPS estimates, and list of stakeholders. Proposed pilot kickoff week of 2026-07-20.

[11:49] Priya: That works. Thanks all.
[11:52] Aisha: Thanks everyone, appreciated.
[11:54] Maya: Thanks — I'll follow up with calendar invites and artifacts. Bye.

End of transcript.
